reviews.text: I took my dog ​​in because he was limping badly, and they told me it was a tendon problem and that he should rest. It turns out he had a piece of glass stuck in his paw pad, and they found it somewhere else. TERRIBLE AND SHAMEFUL!!

Excellent service! We had an emergency, and they took care of her professionally, giving us time to see and pamper her. Her recovery has been so successful; it's almost as if she never had anything wrong. Highly recommended!

ANICURA Velázquez is a veterinary hospital where the professionalism and friendliness of the staff are paramount.
The veterinary care is impeccable. Compared to other veterinary clinics I've visited in Madrid, ANICURA is the one I trust the most. I highly recommend it.

If you love your dog, think twice before taking him to this vet.

I've been taking Whisky to this clinic since he was 3 months old. He's 5 now. For years, he was treated by Dr. Pablo, an excellent professional. Since he left, our experience has completely changed.

For about a year and a half, Whisky has had recurring intestinal problems. He's had numerous tests and analyses, but they never found the cause.

A few months ago, he had a fever and an infection in his anal glands. We took him TWO DAYS IN A ROW because something was clearly wrong. They told us it was probably "his tummy." When we got home, we saw that he had a huge swelling, like a cherry tomato, in the anal area. When we asked how they hadn't noticed it after two appointments, they literally said, "Sorry, I didn't check his bottom these past two days."* It eventually developed into a fistula, and Whisky was very ill, on antibiotic treatment after a diagnosis we believe was incorrect.

We continued trying to find the source of his digestive problems. They even performed a dental cleaning on him, thinking it might be related, but it yielded no results.

Then he started vomiting and passing a lot of blood in his stool. Dr. Diana was one of the few people we saw who seemed genuinely concerned about finding an answer, and in addition to the usual blood work, she ordered folic acid and vitamin B1 levels, which revealed an intestinal abnormality.

And my question is: why, after a year and a half of digestive problems, had these tests never been ordered?

Later, we were told he needed a biopsy. This was decided on August 26th, but we had to wait until September 4th because the person in charge was on vacation. Meanwhile, Whisky continued to suffer from diarrhea and pain. We're talking about a 2.5 kg dog.

Dr. Ignacio, whom I also want to acknowledge, finally performed the endoscopy and took the case with the seriousness we expected.
Afterward, they scheduled an appointment to show us the endoscopy images and explain the results. We were seen by Dr. Paloma, and the experience was, frankly, **unacceptable**.

The first thing she asked us was what kind of food Whisky ate, even though his medical record should state that he doesn't eat kibble, that we've tried more than 12 brands, and that this same clinic referred us to a nutritionist to prepare his diet. Furthermore, we received different and even contradictory instructions compared to those given by other veterinarians who had seen us previously.

Each professional tells us something different, and we're left to try and figure out what to do.

We waited about 30 minutes for a consultation, and to top it all off, they didn't even show us the endoscopy images, even though we had come specifically for that purpose. We didn't need a five-minute consultation. We needed someone to sit down with us and explain what they had found and what was happening with our dog.

Today we have completely lost faith in this clinic and have decided to seek a second opinion elsewhere. We are waiting for the pathology results.
Attention and professionalism

Updated review. Please see the update at the end of this review.

I am a client of Anicura at the Doctor Castelo Clinic, and at the hospital and clinic at Velazquez 105, when necessary.
On July 22nd, I was sent there, as the situation required, for a precautionary x-ray, which fortunately showed that everything was fine and that it was just a severe allergic reaction on his paw.
Jack was seen by José Ignacio, whom I've met on other occasions, with the same care, attention, and professionalism as always.
The explanations were clear, as was the report on Jack's condition and treatment.

José Ignacio is not only a great professional but also a very empathetic and caring person with pets, as is the entire team of assistants at Anicura, and the rest of the veterinarians at all their centers. Congratulations and once again, thank you very much for your help and your kindness.

Two years after this review, and after 14 years of affection, love, licks, and cuddles, Jack passed away three weeks ago. A Westie disease, diagnosed a few days prior, and the passage of time, took him.

Yesterday, I received a heartfelt call from Carmen, the specialist and last veterinarian who cared for Jack. She was an empathetic person and an even better professional, and I thanked her for all her efforts and the diagnosis that allowed us, amidst the pain of our loss, to find peace knowing we had done everything possible, as we had throughout his wonderful life.

Carmen was the final link in the chain that allowed us to care for Jack until his last day and give him a long and happy life. From the first day in Castelo, with Marlene, then Marisa, later Francy, and finally Raul, whom, thanks to Jack's gentle nature, she spared from having to administer the final injection, which I know would have been very difficult. His allergies, and all his treatments, vaccinations, and preventative care, were handled with punctuality and immense love.

Carmen was the last link in the chain that allowed us to care for Jack until his very last day and give him a long and happy life. I haven't forgotten Velazquez, from the reception staff, especially Irene and Tere, Paulo and his dental cleanings, Jose Ignacio and his immense empathy, professionalism, and affection, and Carmen, equally immense in her affection, empathy, and professionalism.

To everyone, thank you, thank you, thank you!!!! We took the best possible care of him, but without you, he wouldn't have made it to 14 years, and he would have left us suddenly without us knowing why. And thank you for organizing everything afterward, the thoughtful touch of the ashes and everything that accompanies them, which allows us to finally rest in peace and remember him always.

If you ever need someone to share their experience with you or simply the perspective of an owner on how to care for, treat, and love a dog, I am at your service. The professionals at Anicura Castelo and Velazquez are no longer just the veterinarians who cared for Jack; they are my friends.

A hug to all from a grateful owner/caregiver.

Pay attention to the dove

The positives: Good, dedicated doctors, good service, and always concerned about the dogs.

The negatives: They need more help. I think they need more doctors and more support for the current doctors. They also need to pay much more attention to cleanliness. It's clear that because they need more help, cleanliness isn't a priority; instead, they're focused on attending to people. There have been days when only one doctor is seeing patients, managing reception, and caring for the hospitalized dogs. The doctors are truly doing their best, but they need help.
The staff are excellent, but they are noticeably overwhelmed. The cleanliness of the place also leaves much to be desired.

During the month we worked with them, they were always available to us. They have specialized veterinarians who helped us diagnose and treat Becky's cancer, provided us with the necessary medication, and were always there for us when we needed them. They also took the time to respectfully explain all the options to us, allowing us to make our own decisions about her treatment.

On the day we had to say goodbye to Becky, the doctor who was with us was incredibly compassionate and loving. Going through such an experience is never easy, but we honestly couldn't have asked for a better team to help us through that process.

After her passing, they also sent us a letter that we still keep and that still moves us when we read it. We are so grateful for the care, respect, and love they gave Becky.

And what can we say about the receptionists and assistants: Sara, Irene, Lucía, Nuria, Macarena, Eva, Karla, and Alba? They are wonderful. Always smiling, always attentive, always ready to help. You can tell they love what they do and do it with care.

My little Moma is seen at Ani Cura by Dr. Carmen, who is wonderful in how she manages her and follows her every step of the way. Sara at reception is also very warm and attentive.
Thank you so much!!

I took her there as an emergency in August because my usual vet was closed. My cat was almost unconscious; she had a tumor that was bleeding heavily. They saved her life. The treatment they gave her is highly specialized, and it shows in the results. They've never been so successful (the technology they must have is more specific and not "general" like in other, smaller clinics). They've also been very attentive, providing continuous follow-up. They're not only true professionals and specialists, but their treatment of owners is also remarkable. The doctor and the assistants are very friendly and caring, reassuring me at all times. I'll always be grateful to them. I recommend this clinic to everyone.

We requested a quote for our dog's neutering, which was sent to us correctly. However, when we called to schedule an appointment and clarify some important questions about the procedure, the service we received from a staff member named Irene was very unsatisfactory.

We asked several questions that required detailed explanations, but the answers we received were simply "yes" or "no," without any further clarification, which made us very distrustful. When we asked her to explain further, she continued to respond in the same way, as if it were an automated process.
